sentences.en: Chelsea Rochman, an ecologist at the University of California, Davis, has been trying to answer a dismal question: Is everything terrible, or are things just very, very bad?
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的生态学家切尔西·罗赫曼一直在试图回答一个令人沮丧的问题：究竟是一切都糟透了，还是情况只是非常、非常糟？

sentences.en: Rochman is a member of the National Center for Ecological Analysis and Synthesis’s marine-debris working group, a collection of scientists who study, among other things, the growing problem of marine debris, also known as ocean trash.
sentences.zh: 罗赫曼是美国国家生态分析与综合中心海洋废弃物工作组的成员。组内科学家的研究对象之一，就是日益严重的海洋废弃物问题，也就是我们常说的海洋垃圾。

sentences.en: Plenty of studies have sounded alarm bells about the state of marine debris; in a recent paper published in the journal Ecology, Rochman and her colleagues set out to determine how many of those perceived risks are real.
sentences.zh: 许多研究都已就海洋废弃物的现状敲响警钟。罗赫曼和同事在最近发表于《生态学》期刊的一篇论文中，着手查明这些被认为存在的风险中有多少确实存在。

sentences.en: Often, Rochman says, scientists will end a paper by speculating about the broader impacts of what they’ve found.
sentences.zh: 罗赫曼说，科学家往往会在论文结尾推测，自己已有的发现可能产生哪些更广泛的影响。

sentences.en: For example, a study could show that certain seabirds eat plastic bags, and go on to warn that whole bird populations are at risk of dying out.
sentences.zh: 例如，一项研究可能发现某些海鸟会吃塑料袋，随后便警告说，整个鸟类种群都面临消亡的风险。

sentences.en: ‘But the truth was that nobody had yet tested those perceived threats,’ Rochman says.
sentences.zh: “但当时的实情是，还没有人检验过这些被认为存在的威胁。”罗赫曼说。

sentences.en: ‘There wasn’t a lot of information.’
sentences.zh: “手头的信息并不多。”

sentences.en: Rochman and her colleagues examined more than a hundred papers on the impacts of marine debris that were published through 2013.
sentences.zh: 罗赫曼和同事们审查了截至2013年已发表的一百多篇有关海洋废弃物影响的论文。

sentences.en: Within each paper, they asked what threats scientists had studied — 366 perceived threats in all — and what they’d actually found.
sentences.zh: 他们逐篇追问，科学家研究了哪些威胁，实际又发现了什么。这些论文提及的潜在威胁共有366项。

sentences.en: In 83 percent of cases, the perceived dangers of ocean trash were proven true.
sentences.zh: 在83%的案例中，人们所担心的海洋垃圾危害得到了证实。

sentences.en: In the remaining cases, the working group found the studies had weaknesses in design and content which affected the validity of their conclusions — they lacked a control group, for example, or used faulty statistics.
sentences.zh: 在其余案例中，工作组发现研究的设计和内容存在缺陷，影响了结论的有效性，例如没有设置对照组，或者使用了有问题的统计方法。

sentences.en: Strikingly, Rochman says, only one well-designed study failed to find the effect it was looking for, an investigation of mussels ingesting microscopic plastic bits.
sentences.zh: 罗赫曼说，值得注意的是，设计严谨却没有发现预期效应的研究只有一项，考察的是贻贝摄入微小塑料碎片后会怎样。

sentences.en: The plastic moved from the mussels’ stomachs to their bloodstreams, scientists found, and stayed there for weeks — but didn’t seem to stress out the shellfish.
sentences.zh: 科学家发现，塑料从贻贝的胃进入其血液循环，并在那里停留数周，却似乎没有让这些贝类出现应激反应。

sentences.en: While mussels may be fine eating trash, though, the analysis also gave a clearer picture of the many ways that ocean debris is bothersome.
sentences.zh: 不过，贻贝吃了垃圾也许没有明显不适，这项分析却也让人们更清楚地看到了海洋废弃物带来危害的多种方式。

sentences.en: Within the studies they looked at, most of the proven threats came from plastic debris, rather than other materials like metal or wood.
sentences.zh: 在他们审查的研究中，多数得到证实的威胁源于塑料废弃物，而非金属或木头等其他材料。

sentences.en: Most of the dangers also involved large pieces of debris — animals getting entangled in trash, for example, or eating it and severely injuring themselves.
sentences.zh: 多数危险还涉及大块垃圾。比如，动物被废弃物缠住，或因吞食废弃物而严重受伤。

sentences.en: But a lot of ocean debris is ‘microplastic’, or pieces smaller than five millimeters.
sentences.zh: 但海洋废弃物中有许多是“微塑料”，也就是小于5毫米的塑料碎片。

sentences.en: These may be ingredients used in cosmetics and toiletries, fibers shed by synthetic clothing in the wash, or eroded remnants of larger debris.
sentences.zh: 这些微塑料可能是化妆品和洗护用品中的成分，也可能是合成纤维衣物在洗涤中脱落的纤维，或较大废弃物磨蚀后留下的碎屑。

sentences.en: Compared to the number of studies investigating large-scale debris, Rochman’s group found little research on the effects of these tiny bits.
sentences.zh: 罗赫曼的研究组发现，与研究大块废弃物的众多论文相比，有关这些微小碎片会造成哪些影响的研究很少。

sentences.en: ‘There are a lot of open questions still for microplastic,’ Rochman says, though she notes that more papers on the subject have been published since 2013, the cutoff point for the group’s analysis.
sentences.zh: “关于微塑料，还有许多悬而未决的问题。”罗赫曼说。不过她也指出，自研究组分析所覆盖的最后一年2013年以来，这一领域又发表了更多论文。

sentences.en: There are also, she adds, a lot of open questions about the ways that ocean debris can lead to sea-creature death.
sentences.zh: 她补充说，关于海洋废弃物究竟通过哪些途径造成海洋生物死亡，同样还有很多问题没有答案。

sentences.en: Many studies have looked at how plastic affects an individual animal, or that animal’s tissues or cells, rather than whole populations.
sentences.zh: 许多研究考察的是塑料怎样影响某个动物个体，或其组织和细胞，考察的对象并非整个种群。

sentences.en: And in the lab, scientists often use higher concentrations of plastic than what’s really in the ocean.
sentences.zh: 而在实验室里，科学家常用的塑料浓度高于海洋中的实际浓度。

sentences.en: None of that tells us how many birds or fish or sea turtles could die from plastic pollution — or how deaths in one species could affect that animal’s predators, or the rest of the ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 这些研究都不能告诉我们，究竟会有多少鸟、鱼或海龟死于塑料污染，也不能告诉我们，一个物种中个体的死亡会怎样影响以它为食的动物，或生态系统的其他部分。

sentences.en: ‘We need to be asking more ecologically relevant questions,’ Rochman says.
sentences.zh: “我们需要问一些更符合生态实际的问题。”罗赫曼说。

sentences.en: Usually, scientists don’t know exactly how disasters such as a tanker accidentally spilling its whole cargo of oil and polluting huge areas of the ocean will affect the environment until after they’ve happened.
sentences.zh: 油轮意外泄漏所载的全部原油、使大片海域受到污染，这类灾难究竟会怎样影响环境，科学家通常要到事后才能弄清楚。

sentences.en: ‘We don’t ask the right questions early enough,’ she says.
sentences.zh: “我们没有及早问对问题。”她说。

sentences.en: But if ecologists can understand how the slow-moving effect of ocean trash is damaging ecosystems, they might be able to prevent things from getting worse.
sentences.zh: 但如果生态学家能弄清海洋垃圾如何在长期的缓慢作用中损害生态系统，或许就能防止情况继续恶化。

sentences.en: Asking the right questions can help policy makers, and the public, figure out where to focus their attention.
sentences.zh: 问对问题，有助于政策制定者和公众弄清应该把注意力集中在哪里。

sentences.en: The problems that look or sound most dramatic may not be the best places to start.
sentences.zh: 视觉或听觉上最惊人的问题，未必最值得先着手解决。

sentences.en: For example, the name of the ‘Great Pacific Garbage Patch’ — a collection of marine debris in the northern Pacific Ocean — might conjure up a vast, floating trash island.
sentences.zh: 比如，“大太平洋垃圾带”这个名字指的是北太平洋聚集着的一批海洋废弃物，却可能让人想象出一座广阔的漂浮垃圾岛。

sentences.en: In reality though, much of the debris is tiny or below the surface; a person could sail through the area without seeing any trash at all.
sentences.zh: 可实际上，其中许多垃圾要么十分细小，要么在水面以下。即使乘船穿过这片海域，也可能什么垃圾都看不到。

sentences.en: A Dutch group called ‘The Ocean Cleanup’ is currently working on plans to put mechanical devices in the Pacific Garbage Patch and similar areas to suck up plastic.
sentences.zh: 一个名为“海洋清理”的荷兰团体正在拟订方案，准备在太平洋垃圾带及类似海域放置机械装置，把塑料吸走。

sentences.en: But a recent paper used simulations to show that strategically positioning the cleanup devices closer to shore would more effectively reduce pollution over the long term.
sentences.zh: 但近期一篇论文通过模拟表明，从长远看，经过谋划将清理装置部署在离海岸更近的地方，能更有效地减轻污染。

sentences.en: ‘I think clearing up some of these misperceptions is really important,’ Rochman says.
sentences.zh: “我认为，澄清其中一些误解非常重要。”罗赫曼说。

sentences.en: Among scientists as well as in the media, she says, ‘A lot of the images about strandings and entanglement and all of that cause the perception that plastic debris is killing everything in the ocean.’
sentences.zh: 她说，无论在科学界还是媒体中，“许多动物搁浅、遭到缠绕之类的画面，都使人们以为塑料废弃物正在杀死海里的一切生物”。

sentences.en: Interrogating the existing scientific literature can help ecologists figure out which problems really need addressing, and which ones they’d be better off — like the mussels — absorbing and ignoring.
sentences.zh: 仔细审视现有科学文献，可以帮助生态学家判断哪些问题确实需要处理，哪些倒不如像贻贝那样，吸收了也不必理会。

questions.question: Rochman and her colleagues were the first people to research the problem of marine debris.
questions.logic: 题干的关键是 first。第2段先说此前已有许多研究发出警告，再用分号引出罗赫曼团队的工作。他们要检验旧研究提出的威胁，已有前人研究就足以否定“最早”。

questions.question: The creatures most in danger from ocean trash are certain seabirds.
questions.logic: 把 most in danger 圈出来。文中举海鸟吃塑料袋为例，只说明海鸟可能面临危险。要得出“危险最大”，还得比较海鸟和其他生物受到的威胁，文中没有给出这个比较。

questions.question: The studies Rochman has reviewed have already proved that populations of some birds will soon become extinct.
questions.logic: 区分观察、推测和证实。研究可能观察到海鸟吃塑料袋，再警告整个种群有灭绝风险。作者紧接着明确说这种威胁当时尚未经过检验，这与题干的 already proved 直接矛盾。

questions.question: Rochman analysed papers on the different kinds of danger caused by ocean trash.
questions.logic: 找罗赫曼实际做的工作。她们回顾了截至2013年发表的一百多篇论文，并逐篇追问研究了哪些威胁、实际发现了什么。文中的366种假定威胁，正好说明分析涉及不同类型的危险。

questions.question: Most of the research analysed by Rochman and her colleagues was badly designed.
questions.logic: 核对 most 的分母。83%的案例证实了原先担心的危害，设计或方法缺陷出现在余下那部分案例中。题干把这个较小的范围扩大成“大部分研究”。

questions.question: One study examined by Rochman was expecting to find that mussels were harmed by eating plastic.
questions.logic: 题干问的是研究者预期看到什么。原文把贻贝研究列为“没有发现预期效应”的例子。预计摄入塑料会伤害贻贝，实际却未观察到明显应激，这两个时间点要分开。

questions.question: Some mussels choose to eat plastic in preference to their natural diet.
questions.logic: 实验观察了贻贝摄入塑料后的生理反应。题干的 in preference to 要求有选择行为，例如同时提供天然食物和塑料，再比较贻贝怎样选。文中没有报告这种试验或偏好。

questions.question: bits of debris that were ______ (harmful to animals)
questions.logic: 题干先用 materials 区分塑料、金属和木头，下一行转而问碎片的特征。去找缠住动物或造成重伤的例子，原文的 large pieces 把尺寸说清了。were 后填原文形容词 large。

questions.question: There was little research into ______ e.g. from synthetic fibres.
questions.logic: synthetic fibres 是来源线索。原文把这些小于五毫米的碎片归入 microplastic，又说研究其影响的论文很少。题目问缺少研究的材料类别，应取这个总称。

questions.question: most of them focused on individual animals, not entire ______
questions.logic: 看 individual animals 与 entire 之间的层级对照。原文从组织、细胞和动物个体转到整个种群，对应词是复数 populations。这里不涉及整个生态系统。

questions.question: the ______ of plastic used in the lab did not always reflect those in the ocean
questions.logic: 比较的是实验室与海洋中的同一个量。原文说实验常用更高的塑料浓度，题干的 those 回指这个复数量。照录 concentrations，别把材料名称 plastic 再填一次。

questions.question: - the impact of a reduction in numbers on the ______ of that species
questions.logic: 先确定食物链方向。题目问某物种数量减少会影响谁，原文写 that animal’s predators，即以该物种为食的捕食者。prey 会把谁吃谁颠倒。

questions.question: Rochman says more information is needed on the possible impact of future ______ (e.g. involving oil).
questions.logic: 括号里的油是例子。原文以油轮泄漏说明科学家常常要等灾难发生后才知道其影响。题目要求的是这类事件的上位词，填 disasters。

questions.question: What would be the best title for this passage?
questions.chosen_text: Assessing the threat of marine debris

options.A: Assessing the threat of marine debris
options.B: Marine debris: who is to blame?
options.C: A new solution to the problem of marine debris
options.D: Marine debris: the need for international action

questions.logic: 通读时抓住贯穿全文的问题：研究者核查哪些威胁已被证实、现有研究有什么局限、下一步应查什么。A 同时覆盖这三点。B 要追究责任，C 只对应文末的一项清理设想，D 要求国际行动，三者都不能概括全文。

grammar.heading: 两个并列的宾语从句
grammar.analysis: 主干是 they asked。what threats scientists had studied 与 what they’d actually found 都受 asked 支配。两个破折号间的数字补充说明前一项的数量；actually 把“研究了什么”与“实际发现什么”区分开。
grammar.pattern: The review examined what … and what … actually …
grammar.task: Task 2 · 评价政府资助的就业培训
grammar.example: The review examined what skills the courses promised to teach and what participants could actually do six months later.
grammar.example_zh: 这项评估考察了课程承诺教授哪些技能，以及参加者六个月后实际具备哪些能力。
grammar.usage: 两个 what 各自带陈述句语序。写涉及承诺与效果的比较时，第二项要能够被观察或测量。

grammar.heading: 否定范围覆盖两个问题
grammar.analysis: 主干是 None of that tells us …，that 指前面提到的研究。第一个 how many 问可能死亡的个体数量，第二个 how 问个体死亡怎样影响捕食者和生态系统。or 连接两项，句首的否定对两项都有效。
grammar.pattern: These figures tell us neither how many … nor how …
grammar.task: Task 1 · 说明一张地铁进站人次图表的局限
grammar.example: These figures tell us neither how many different people used the metro nor how their journeys were distributed across the day.
grammar.example_zh: 这些数字既无法说明有多少不同的人乘坐地铁，也无法说明他们的行程在一天中如何分布。
grammar.usage: 人次不能自动推出人数或时段；不要把图上没有统计的量当成数据变化趋势。

grammar.heading: 动名词短语充当从句主语
grammar.analysis: 主句是 a recent paper used simulations。to show 引出模拟的用途，that 从句里的主语是 strategically positioning the cleanup devices closer to shore，谓语是 would … reduce。closer to shore 修饰设备放置的位置。
grammar.pattern: A simulation suggests that placing [设施] closer to [地点] could [效果].
grammar.task: Task 2 · 优化社区回收点的布局
grammar.example: A simulation could test whether placing recycling bins closer to apartment entrances would increase participation.
grammar.example_zh: 可以用模拟来检验，把回收箱设在更靠近公寓入口的地方是否会提高参与率。
grammar.usage: 情境只提出研究设想，所以用 could test whether。得到结果后才适合写结果支持哪个判断。
